name: Iyayu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only 2 Glottolog refs, both overview/socling (Jungraithmayr & Ganslmayr 1986; Oyebade & Agoyi 2004); no descriptive phonology exists.

new_statements.quote: p.58: "Systematic Phonetic Tones in Ìyàyú. A careful examination of Ìyàyú dialect systematic phonetic level reveals that the dialect has high, low and mid tones. i. The high tone is realized phonetically in Ìyàyú dialect. It can be found in word initial, medial and final positions ..." p.60: "The study also found out that Ìyàyú is a tonal language with three functional pitch levels. They are High [ ́ ], Mid [ ], and Low [ ̀ ]. These tones are functionally load-carriers. They are used lexically and grammatically for distinguishing words which are segmentally identical."
new_statements.citation: Àìná-Adébáyò, Olúwátóyìn Bọ̀sẹ̀dé; Adébáyọ̀, Tayo; Ìgè, Oluwatoyin Dayo. 2026. Aspects of the phonology of Ìyàyú dialect in Ìdó-Àní, Ondo State. International Journal of Arts, Languages, Linguistics and Literary Studies (JOLLS) 15(1): 48-62. DOI 10.4314/jolls.v15i1.5.
new_statements.locator: p.58, section 'Systematic Phonetic Tones in Ìyàyú'; p.60, Discussion of findings (PDF pp.11 and 13)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Iyayu is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L) with lexical and grammatical (tense-marking) tone; the article gives no statement about word stress or accent anywhere (the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone: H, M, L all occur word-initially, medially and finally; tone distinguishes present/continuous vs past.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone illustrated on isolated words (SIL 1700-item wordlist elicitation from 30 speakers aged 60+) and a few sentence pairs; syllable types V and CV only, no codas or clusters.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes the speech of Ìyàyú quarter of Ìdó-Àní (Ido-Ani) town, Ọ̀sẹ́ LGA, Ondo State — exactly Glottolog iyay1238 (alt. name Idoani). The authors call it a 'dialect' but treat it as an Edoid (North-Western Edoid) lect not mutually intelligible with the Yoruba-like speech of the other five quarters; oral tradition links the group to Sósan (Akoko South-East), matching Glottolog's 'Sosan = Iyayu' mapping for Oyebade & Agoyi 2004.

States Iyayu is a tonal language with three level tones H, M, L (p.58 'Systematic Phonetic Tones in Ìyàyú'; p.60 summary), tone has lexical and grammatical (tense) function; syllables V and CV only, open syllables.
